text:
Megan (acct-exec): Hey team — FinTrust POC next week. They want PrivateDeploy inside their VPC but will route traffic through their on-prem proxy (opaque tunnel). They asked: can Redwood preserve client source IP, pass SNI through, and what firewall rules/ports they must open? Also curious on cost differences between PrivateLink vs VPC peering for steady 200 Mbps traffic.

Raj (netops): Short answers up front: 1) VPC peering preserves client src IP (traffic is L3). 2) PrivateLink (interface endpoint) will appear from our ENIs — you won't see original client IP unless the proxy inserts X-Forwarded-For. 3) SNI depends on TLS termination: if TLS is terminated in their proxy for inspection, SNI may be removed or replaced.

Lisa (solutions): Additional nuance: with PrivateLink we terminate on an ENI in the customer's subnet, so their firewall will see our service IPs. If the customer needs original client IP for routing/policies, recommend VPC peering or put an explicit NAT/forwarder on their side that preserves headers.

Eve (security): From a compliance POV FinTrust wants audit logs with client IPs. If they can't get src IP via PrivateLink we can add request-level headers (X-Forwarded-For) in the runtime, but note that header attestation depends on trusting the proxy. Would prefer VPC peering or a small packet mirroring setup for IDS.

Sam (eng-runtime): Tech constraints: we can emit X-Forwarded-For and/or a Signed-Client header. We cannot magically recover original src IP if network path NATs it away. Also, function/tool-calling and streaming unaffected. Code-level example of headers we add: 
```
X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.42
X-Redwood-Signed: v1:eyJhbGci...
```

Raj (netops): Firewall snippet (customer side) — allow outbound to Redwood ENI range (example) and standard HTTPS: 
```
# allow to Redwood endpoints and healthchecks
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to 100.64.10.0/24 ports 443, 80
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to 198.51.100.0/28 ports 1024-65535 # callback/ephemeral
```
Replace with actual ranges we provide in handoff doc.

Megan (acct-exec): Raj — can you confirm exact egress IP block we hand off for POC? FinTrust's firewall team wants a CIDR.

infra-bot: Temporary POC env created: redwood-poc-fintrust-2025, egress host range: 100.64.10.0/24 (placeholder). Update will follow after environment provisioning.

Raj (netops): Confirming: for the Dedicated POC we'll allocate static EIPs if they want a fixed public egress. For PrivateDeploy inside their VPC + PrivateLink, our ENIs are in their subnet and there is no public EIP; they see our ENI IPs (private). If they want single public IP for outbound, use NAT gateway on their side.

Lisa (solutions): Cost note: PrivateLink has per-hour+per-GB charges on AWS (interface endpoint hourly + data processing). For 200 Mbps sustained, VPC peering or TGW is usually cheaper. PrivateLink is fine for compliance/isolation when volumes are modest.

Eve (security): One more: if they plan TLS inspection, we need to agree on header attestation and rekey processes. Also confirm KMS/HSM access patterns for logs. I'll prepare a short questionnaire for FinTrust to sign off.

Megan (acct-exec): Thanks — can someone draft a minimal checklist I can send to their firewall team? Needs: CIDRs, ports, DNS / DoH guidance, and whether they must preserve SNI.

Raj (netops): Draft checklist (send as-is, replace placeholder CIDRs):
- Network mode: VPC peering (recommended for src IP) OR PrivateLink (recommended for minimal customer infra)
- If using PrivateLink: open subnet for Redwood ENIs, allow TCP 443 inbound to ENI range 100.64.10.0/24
- If peering: allow 10.0.0.0/16 <-> 10.1.0.0/16 (example) internal TCP 443 and ephemeral ports 1024-65535 for streaming callbacks
- DNS: use customer's resolver; if using PrivateLink with a DNS override, allow queries to resolver IPs. If the customer uses DoH, ensure proxy forwards DNS appropriately.
- SNI/Inspect: if TLS-inspect, expect SNI to be lost or mutated — recommend passing X-Forwarded-For and Signed-Client header for audit
- Egress IPs: if public egress required for allowlisting, customer should configure NAT to single EIP or request static EIPs from Redwood Dedicated (we can allocate on request)

Megan (acct-exec): Perfect. I'll send to FinTrust and loop back their firewall engineer. Sam — assign an engineer to validate X-Forwarded-For header behavior with their proxy?

Sam (eng-runtime): I'll put this on Marcus's plate and we'll run a quick test harness with an opaque TLS proxy. Expect a response within 24h.

Megan (acct-exec): Awesome, thanks all :thumbsup:
